pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented against his own body — overhead swings starting light because of the shoulder, whole-body work for the back, and a daily five-to-fifteen-minute mobility routine that could sit between poker hands. His reaction was the most positive in the batch: 'Of course. Yeah. Yes. I know this is the program. Like, I'm 100% sure.' Volunteered, unqualified, and tied straight back to the problem he came with.

He co-built this pillar rather than receiving it. Told the when/what/how-much frame he immediately matched it to his own practice — 'I fast, I eat between one and two, and then between eight and nine at night. So that's my eight hour window' — and then went further than the rep, volunteering 'what I want to do is I want to eat one ingredient foods' and reasoning it out with the rice-versus-potato example. He also framed keto as a temporary detox before transitioning to whole foods, which is exactly the destination the rep was describing. The longest and most engaged nutrition exchange in the batch.

The pillar that closed him, because it landed directly on a scar. He had already described being injured by a generic online programme with no feedback — 'how could I know if my form was right or wrong if I'm just following a video? And I got hurt' — so the filmed-workout form review answered a specific, personal failure: 'if I can film myself and send it to Trevor, and then he'll say, hey, when you're squatting, your knee is going forward, you shouldn't do that.' He then pre-committed unprompted: 'my commitment with Trevor is I'll show up every day. No excuses. If it's a five-day program, I'll show up every single day.' And asked what mattered most of the three, he chose this one: 'I just want to feel that there's someone supporting me through this journey.'

anchors.raw: I got shredded, I did this calisthenic program, which was an online program by Frank Medrano... It just felt like you just put everything, your weight, your height, and then you pay and then they just send you a program, but it's not personalized.
anchors.note: The most valuable anchor in the batch and the only genuinely supportive one of its kind. He has already bought the cheap generic alternative, got a result from it, and then got injured by it — so the premium's differentiator, personalisation and form feedback, is something he has already paid to learn the hard way. The rep spotted this and leaned on it. This is the answer to the 'cheaper alternative that worked' gap that defeats reps elsewhere in this batch: find the prospect's own bad experience with the substitute.

anchors.raw: And this is a one-time payment? Or is it monthly payment? / It's a one-time fee. / Okay. Sounds good.
anchors.note: $6,000 accepted in a single exchange with no negotiation, no plan requested and no financial discussion at any point. Corroborated by a poker income he lives on, a separate office, and international travel. The rep did not need to run a money play and correctly did not try.

anchors.raw: I'm going to Dallas in September. I'm gonna go see this doctor, the ring dinger, super viral dude, so I'm just trying to try new stuff
anchors.note: Ambiguous but net supportive. He is already committed to flying internationally and paying for an intervention on the same problem, which proves both willingness to spend on his back and an active search for a solution. It is also a competing explanation of where the fix comes from, and nobody asked what the trip costs or how the two approaches interact — a missed chance to position the programme as the durable answer versus a one-off adjustment.

anchors.raw: I see these ads on Insta, like, be ripped in 28 days, and I'm like, dude, this is physically impossible
anchors.note: He rejects the cheap end of the category on credibility before price is ever mentioned, and separately says 'I know it involves effort, time, discipline, it's money, because it's not free'. He arrived expecting to pay, which is the inverse of the Richard Kellis call the same day where the prospect expected $30 a month.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that he can perform overhead kettlebell work with a shoulder that currently cannot go through a full lateral or overhead range without pain
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised this as his central doubt — 'it's hard for me to believe that I can grab a kettlebell with the pain that I feel when I do these exercises' — and the answer was reassurance rather than assessment: Trevor has had shoulder injuries too, and we will start light. Nobody established what the shoulder actually is, whether it has been examined, or whether overhead loading is appropriate. The rep also asserted the training would fix it, which is a clinical claim about an undiagnosed restriction.

unmet_demand.want: A resolution to several years of chronic lower back pain, severe enough that he is flying to Dallas in September for chiropractic treatment
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The pain was well quantified in discovery and then folded into the sales narrative — the daily mobility routine 'directly going to help with suppressing the pain with, well, the mobility, because it actually fixes it'. That is a therapeutic claim about a multi-year condition under no assessment, made to a prospect who is simultaneously seeking medical intervention for it. Whether the two approaches conflict was never discussed.

unmet_demand.want: Help with daily smoking, which he identifies as the direct cause of the cravings that break his diet
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He volunteered it plainly — 'if I don't smoke, then I get no cravings at all... if I smoke, I'll get the munchies' — and the rep probed only the frequency, in the context of dietary discipline, then moved on. The nutrition protocol makes no mention of it, and it is the single behavioural lever he himself named as controlling his adherence.

unmet_demand.want: A programme he actively enjoys, since he abandons regimes that work but are not enjoyable
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He said it twice, including about carnivore — 'I feel great, but I'm not enjoying the process of feeling great' — and 'during this whole process with Trevor, I want to enjoy the process'. The rep addressed the nutrition half convincingly (whole foods, not chicken and rice, sustainable) but never addressed whether the training itself would be enjoyable. Probably served, since he chose kettlebells partly out of curiosity, but it is his documented failure mode and nobody closed it off.
